In summary, our research is concerned with
a new technique for unilateral posterior instrumentation.
the development of a new spinal implant, the CLARIS, and the study of its biomechanical behavior.
the study of the biomechanics of the spine, in particular the behavior of the L3–L5 segment in the lumbar spine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unilateral instrumentation is a good alternative for the posterior fixation of the lumbar spine.
unilateral instrumentation is a viable option for the treatment of lumbar degenerative disc disease.
the biomechanical behavior of the instrumented segment with CLARIS is similar in all situations with regard to the intact segment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
unilateral pedicle screw system can be used in the lumbar spine, with a slight reduction of ROM in comparison to a bilateral system.
unilateral instrumentation with CLARIS cage could be an alternative to bilateral instrumentation with CLARSI cage for the L3-L5 motion segment in lumbar spine surgery.
unilateral CLARIS fixation induces a slight increase of ROM in lateral bending and a slight decrease of ROM in axial rotation and flexion-extension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unilateral CLARIS fixation is an effective alternative to bilateral fixation in the treatment of L3-L4 degenerative disc disease.
unilateral instrumentation is as efficient as bilateral instrumentation.
unilateral instrumentation is a viable option for fusion cage with or without posterior instrumentation.
